title: A Break for Kit

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit wants to finish a long block road, but he is tired; after dropping another block he chooses a break, then returns for the final gap.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Kit keeps carrying blocks despite feeling tired and drops the next block beside the unfinished road.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit chooses when to sit and when to return; he places the last block and sends his truck along the completed road.

setting: Ordinary classroom floor in daylight; low block road crosses a green rug; one low wooden seat beside the rug. Kit and Zoe retain the locked cast clothing.
props: Eight large tan rectangular blocks forming one road
One small red toy truck
One low wooden seat
One green rug
coverBrief: Kit sits comfortably on the low seat beside an almost complete block road. His red truck rests on the rug; Zoe kneels by the far end. Emphasize his deliberate pause, not illness, collapse or adult permission.

pages.text: Kit wants a long road for his truck.
pages.imageBrief: Kit carries a tan block toward a short straight road on the green rug; Zoe kneels at its far end. The red truck waits near Kit. Continuity: Road has four blocks in place; four loose blocks remain; truck is stationary.
pages.imageAlt: Kit carries a tan block toward a short straight road on the green rug; Zoe kneels at its far end. The red truck waits near Kit.
pages.pageDescription: Kit carries a tan block toward a short straight road on the green rug; Zoe kneels at its far end. The red truck waits near Kit.
pages.state: Road has four blocks in place; four loose blocks remain; truck is stationary.

pages.text:
He carries more blocks.
His arms feel tired.
pages.imageBrief: Kit sets the sixth road block down and lets his arms hang for a moment. Zoe watches without taking his blocks or directing him. Continuity: Six blocks form the road; two loose blocks remain near Kit.
pages.imageAlt: Kit sets the sixth road block down and lets his arms hang for a moment. Zoe watches without taking his blocks or directing him.
pages.pageDescription: Kit sets the sixth road block down and lets his arms hang for a moment. Zoe watches without taking his blocks or directing him.
pages.state: Six blocks form the road; two loose blocks remain near Kit.

pages.text:
Kit picks up another block.
It slips onto the rug.
pages.imageBrief: The seventh block has landed flat on the soft rug beside Kit’s shoes. His empty hands are still above it; no block hits anyone. Continuity: Six road blocks; seventh lies beside road; eighth remains loose. No injury.
pages.imageAlt: The seventh block has landed flat on the soft rug beside Kit’s shoes. His empty hands are still above it; no block hits anyone.
pages.pageDescription: The seventh block has landed flat on the soft rug beside Kit’s shoes. His empty hands are still above it; no block hits anyone.
pages.state: Six road blocks; seventh lies beside road; eighth remains loose. No injury.

pages.text:
“I need a break,” says Kit.
He sits down.
pages.imageBrief: Kit sits on the low seat with both hands resting on his knees. Zoe remains beside the unfinished road; she is not blocking or beckoning him. Continuity: Kit initiates the pause. Dropped block and final loose block remain on the rug.
pages.imageAlt: Kit sits on the low seat with both hands resting on his knees. Zoe remains beside the unfinished road; she is not blocking or beckoning him.
pages.pageDescription: Kit sits on the low seat with both hands resting on his knees. Zoe remains beside the unfinished road; she is not blocking or beckoning him.
pages.state: Kit initiates the pause. Dropped block and final loose block remain on the rug.

pages.text:
Zoe adds one block.
Kit watches from his seat.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe lifts the dropped seventh block into the road. Kit sits nearby, looking toward the construction; the last loose block remains beside the small gap. Continuity: Seven blocks now placed; eighth remains loose; Kit still rests.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe lifts the dropped seventh block into the road. Kit sits nearby, looking toward the construction; the last loose block remains beside the small gap.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe lifts the dropped seventh block into the road. Kit sits nearby, looking toward the construction; the last loose block remains beside the small gap.
pages.state: Seven blocks now placed; eighth remains loose; Kit still rests.

pages.text:
Kit rests a little longer.
The last gap stays open.
pages.imageBrief: Quiet side view: Kit has leaned comfortably against the seat back, hands loose. The road has one clearly visible block-sized gap before its final turn. Continuity: No new blocks placed; one gap and one loose block persist; Zoe waits beside the truck.
pages.imageAlt: Quiet side view: Kit has leaned comfortably against the seat back, hands loose. The road has one clearly visible block-sized gap before its final turn.
pages.pageDescription: Quiet side view: Kit has leaned comfortably against the seat back, hands loose. The road has one clearly visible block-sized gap before its final turn.
pages.state: No new blocks placed; one gap and one loose block persist; Zoe waits beside the truck.

pages.text:
Kit gets up.
“I want to put that one in.”
pages.imageBrief: Kit stands and reaches toward the eighth block with relaxed shoulders. Zoe moves her hands away, leaving the choice and action to him. Continuity: Kit has chosen to return; final block is not placed yet.
pages.imageAlt: Kit stands and reaches toward the eighth block with relaxed shoulders. Zoe moves her hands away, leaving the choice and action to him.
pages.pageDescription: Kit stands and reaches toward the eighth block with relaxed shoulders. Zoe moves her hands away, leaving the choice and action to him.
pages.state: Kit has chosen to return; final block is not placed yet.

pages.text:
He fills the gap.
His truck rolls all the way.
pages.imageBrief: Kit pushes the small red truck along the now continuous eight-block road. Zoe watches from the other end; the empty seat remains beside the rug. Continuity: All eight blocks form the road; no loose blocks; Kit’s chosen return completes the original goal.
pages.imageAlt: Kit pushes the small red truck along the now continuous eight-block road. Zoe watches from the other end; the empty seat remains beside the rug.
pages.pageDescription: Kit pushes the small red truck along the now continuous eight-block road. Zoe watches from the other end; the empty seat remains beside the rug.
pages.state: All eight blocks form the road; no loose blocks; Kit’s chosen return completes the original goal.

oral.prompt: What did Kit choose after the block slipped?
oral.listenFor: He chose to sit and rest, then chose to return for the last block. Stopping briefly did not mean giving up the road.

visual.prompt: What is waiting while Kit rests?
visual.lookFor: The last loose block and the one gap in the road; nobody has finished his remaining part for him.

levelRationale: Candidate B: Short present-tense actions and two dialogue pages track one familiar goal. The pause has an observable consequence and a chosen return; no general medical or learning-style claim is made.

languagePrep.meaning: a short time to stop and rest
an empty space between things

title: The Saved Cracker

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit eats a cracker Zoe set aside for her snack; his first offer is unsuitable, so he asks what she wants and replaces it with his own saved cracker.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Kit offers a loose crumb after taking the whole cracker; Zoe’s empty plate and reply show why that does not restore her snack.
storyBibleReview.resolution: With Zoe’s agreement, Kit gives her the untouched cracker from his own lunch box; she can finish her planned snack.

setting: Classroom snack table, two chairs, clean tabletop. Only Kit and Zoe; all food is already prepared.
props: One small white plate with a blue rim for Zoe
Two identical square crackers: Zoe’s on her plate and Kit’s untouched in his box
One yellow lunch box for Kit
One small piece of cheese on Zoe’s plate
A few crumbs after Kit eats
coverBrief: Zoe looks at her blue-rimmed plate, which holds cheese but no cracker. Kit holds his open yellow lunch box with one untouched square cracker visible. Show the specific missing snack, without angry caricatures.

pages.text:

She gets a cup.

pages.imageAlt: Kit holds one tiny crumb above the table. Zoe leaves her hands beside her plate and gently shakes her head.
pages.pageDescription: Kit holds one tiny crumb above the table. Zoe leaves her hands beside her plate and gently shakes her head.

Kit opens his box.

pages.imageBrief: Kit lifts the yellow box lid, revealing his own untouched square cracker. Zoe’s plate remains beside the box, still lacking a cracker. Continuity: Only the second, original cracker is whole; no new food appears.

pages.pageDescription: Kit lifts the yellow box lid, revealing his own untouched square cracker. Zoe’s plate remains beside the box, still lacking a cracker.

“Would you like mine?” asks Kit.
“Yes,” says Zoe.

pages.pageDescription: Kit places his untouched cracker next to Zoe’s cheese. His yellow lunch box is now empty.

Zoe puts the cheese on top.
This bite has a cracker.

oral.prompt: Why did the crumb not fix Zoe’s problem?
oral.listenFor: She had saved a whole cracker to hold her cheese. Kit asked and replaced it with his own whole cracker.

visual.prompt: Where did the replacement cracker come from?
visual.lookFor: Kit’s yellow box is empty now; the same untouched cracker has moved to Zoe’s plate.

levelRationale: Candidate B: A concrete object remains the goal throughout; brief dialogue occurs on two pages. Taking, impact, an inadequate attempt and agreed repair are all printed rather than left only to faces.

title: A Letter Finds Zoe

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How does Kit’s letter reach Zoe?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one sealed cream envelope from addressing and collection through sorting, transport and final delivery to its recipient.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The picture reaches Zoe because the address links several workers’ stages of the journey.

scienceSources.title: Smithsonian National Postal Museum: Mail Processing
scienceSources.evidence: Indexed primary museum text checked: collection, facing/cancellation, sorting, transport to destination office and carrier delivery to the correct address. Later direct open was blocked; the complete indexed explanation was available. The illustrated route is one example, not a universal promise.

scienceSources.title: Smithsonian National Postal Museum: Systems at Work resources
scienceSources.evidence: Primary museum account describes collection, transport to a sorting facility, belts/rollers, address reading and division by destination. Supports machine sorting without requiring children to read a real address.

setting: Illustrative ordinary postal route from Kit’s home through a sorting center to Zoe’s home. No named postal operator, flags, logos or exact delivery-time claim. Addresses face away or appear as ruled lines, not fabricated readable personal data.
props: One cream envelope with a small green star postage stamp at upper right
One folded picture of a red toy truck inside
One blue collection box
Gray mail trays and one plain delivery van
Zoe’s blue front door with a mail slot
Collection worker: tan skin, short brown hair, navy shirt and gray trousers
Carrier: brown skin, short black hair, pale blue shirt and navy trousers
coverBrief: The carrier holds the cream envelope beside Zoe’s blue door; Zoe reaches for it. The small green star stamp identifies the same letter, with no visible address wording.

Kit puts a picture in an envelope.

pages.imageAlt: Kit posts the sealed cream envelope into the slot of a plain blue collection box. Its green star stamp is visible, address turned away.

oral.prompt: What helped the letter reach the right home?
oral.listenFor: The address guided sorting and the carrier’s final delivery. Several jobs connected Kit’s picture to Zoe.

levelRationale: Candidate B: Each short page advances one familiar object along a concrete route. Three postal terms are supported orally; syntax remains simple and the ending returns to the opening picture.

title: The Swapping Clips

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Magic clips exchange the colors of the two objects they grip; Kit makes his cart red using Zoe’s cup, then must restore her cup and obtain permission for another red object.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: The first swap colors Zoe’s cup blue. Kit gets the cart color he wanted but interferes with her cup.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit reverses the first swap, asks to use red paper and makes his cart red while Zoe keeps her red cup.

setting: Ordinary classroom play table. Explicit fantasy: two silver clips connected by one green cord exchange only the overall colors of the two clipped objects; nothing changes size, shape or ownership. Clips themselves and people never change color. Each exchange happens once when the second clip is fastened; removing and fastening the pair again reverses it. The colors do not keep oscillating while clips remain attached.
props: Two silver spring clips joined by a green cord
One plain blue wooden toy cart, becoming red after swaps
Zoe’s plain red cup, briefly blue then restored
One red sheet of paper, ultimately blue
coverBrief: Kit clips the blue cart and a red sheet of paper with the connected silver clips. Zoe holds her restored red cup nearby. The central visual is the two ordinary objects linked by the magical cord, not sparkles or a new magical character.

pages.text:
The magic clips swap colors.
A red cup. A blue cart.
pages.imageBrief: Kit holds two connected silver clips beside Zoe’s red cup and his blue cart, ready to attach them. The red paper lies unused farther back. Continuity: Before first swap: cup red, cart blue, paper red; clips still free, silver; cord green.
pages.imageAlt: Kit holds two connected silver clips beside Zoe’s red cup and his blue cart, ready to attach them. The red paper lies unused farther back.
pages.pageDescription: Kit holds two connected silver clips beside Zoe’s red cup and his blue cart, ready to attach them. The red paper lies unused farther back.

pages.text:
Kit clips both. His cart turns red.
Her cup turns blue.
pages.imageBrief: The clipped cup is now solid blue and the clipped cart solid red; Kit leans toward his cart. The same red sheet remains untouched. Continuity: First swap complete; object shapes unchanged. No extra cups or carts.
pages.imageAlt: The clipped cup is now solid blue and the clipped cart solid red; Kit leans toward his cart. The same red sheet remains untouched.
pages.pageDescription: The clipped cup is now solid blue and the clipped cart solid red; Kit leans toward his cart. The same red sheet remains untouched.
pages.state: First swap complete; object shapes unchanged. No extra cups or carts.

pages.text:
Zoe reaches for her cup.
“That is not my red cup!”
pages.imageBrief: Zoe pauses with an outstretched hand at her now blue cup; Kit looks at it. The clips remain attached to cup and cart. Continuity: Her reaction identifies the social effect; cup blue, cart red, paper red.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe pauses with an outstretched hand at her now blue cup; Kit looks at it. The clips remain attached to cup and cart.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe pauses with an outstretched hand at her now blue cup; Kit looks at it. The clips remain attached to cup and cart.
pages.state: Her reaction identifies the social effect; cup blue, cart red, paper red.

pages.text:
Kit swaps them back.
Zoe takes her red cup.
pages.imageBrief: Kit has unclipped and reclipped the same two objects to trigger the reverse exchange; Zoe lifts the restored red cup after he removes its clip. Continuity: Cup red again; cart blue again; paper red. Both clips are now free.
pages.imageAlt: Kit has unclipped and reclipped the same two objects to trigger the reverse exchange; Zoe lifts the restored red cup after he removes its clip.
pages.pageDescription: Kit has unclipped and reclipped the same two objects to trigger the reverse exchange; Zoe lifts the restored red cup after he removes its clip.
pages.state: Cup red again; cart blue again; paper red. Both clips are now free.

pages.text:
Kit still wants a red cart.
He finds red paper.
pages.imageBrief: Kit sets the blue cart beside the unused red paper and looks toward Zoe. Zoe keeps her red cup out of the clipping area. Continuity: No swap yet; paper remains red; Kit has not taken it without asking.
pages.imageAlt: Kit sets the blue cart beside the unused red paper and looks toward Zoe. Zoe keeps her red cup out of the clipping area.
pages.pageDescription: Kit sets the blue cart beside the unused red paper and looks toward Zoe. Zoe keeps her red cup out of the clipping area.
pages.state: No swap yet; paper remains red; Kit has not taken it without asking.

“May I use this?”
Zoe slides the paper over.
pages.imageBrief: Kit points at the red sheet. Zoe slides it across the table to him, with her red cup held in her other hand. Continuity: Permission granted for paper; cup remains red and excluded from new swap.

pages.pageDescription: Kit points at the red sheet. Zoe slides it across the table to him, with her red cup held in her other hand.

Kit clips the blue cart and red paper.

Kit rolls his red cart.

oral.prompt: Why did Kit swap the cup and cart back?
oral.listenFor: The first change affected Zoe’s cup. He restored it, then asked to use a different red object.

visual.prompt: Which three objects now have different or unchanged colors?

levelRationale: Candidate B: The same three props carry a reversible rule and a visible social consequence. Two dialogue pages and short color/action clauses keep the causal sequence within B; it is explicitly magic, not a claim about color science.

title: A Pool Left Behind

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Why does water remain in a rock pool after the sea has fallen?
storyBibleReview.progression: Observe the same rock hollow across a falling tide, isolated low-tide pool and returning tide; distinguish water held by the hollow from surrounding exposed rock.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The rock hollow holds seawater during low tide and reconnects with the sea as water rises.

scienceSources.title: NOAA Ocean Service: What is a tide pool?
scienceSources.evidence: Defines a tide pool as an isolated seawater pocket in the intertidal zone and describes exposure as ocean water retreats at low tide and renewal at high tide. The book follows one intact rock hollow, not every possible shore depression.

setting: One temperate rocky shore over several hours. View from seaward toward a low rock shelf with a deep oval hollow, a white vein in its left rim and one dark upright boulder behind. No children or animals are required; not a series of different pools.
props: One oval rock hollow with a continuous rim
One white mineral vein in left rim
One dark boulder behind the pool
Sea water with a believable changing level
coverBrief: The oval hollow holds clear seawater while the surrounding rock shelf is exposed. Beyond its lower rim, the sea lies visibly farther down the shore. White vein and dark boulder anchor the place.

pages.text: Sea water covers a dip in rock.
pages.imageBrief: At higher tide, clear seawater extends continuously across the rock shelf and its oval hollow; submerged rim and white vein are visible below the surface. Continuity: Same hollow underwater, connected to sea on every side; boulder stands partly above water.
pages.imageAlt: At higher tide, clear seawater extends continuously across the rock shelf and its oval hollow; submerged rim and white vein are visible below the surface.
pages.pageDescription: At higher tide, clear seawater extends continuously across the rock shelf and its oval hollow; submerged rim and white vein are visible below the surface.
pages.state: Same hollow underwater, connected to sea on every side; boulder stands partly above water.

pages.text:
Slowly, the sea falls.
The rock begins to show.
pages.imageBrief: Water level has lowered enough to uncover the high parts of the rim. The lower side still connects the hollow to the surrounding sea. Continuity: Falling tide over time, not one receding wave; boulder unchanged.
pages.imageAlt: Water level has lowered enough to uncover the high parts of the rim. The lower side still connects the hollow to the surrounding sea.
pages.pageDescription: Water level has lowered enough to uncover the high parts of the rim. The lower side still connects the hollow to the surrounding sea.

title: Wheels for Mars

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can a Mars rover cross rough ground without a smooth road?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one illustrative small-rock crossing by the front, middle and rear wheels on one side, while the articulated suspension changes position.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Six wheels linked by movable supports let the rover cross uneven ground rather than requiring a flat road.

scienceSources.title: NASA: Perseverance Rover Components, Wheels and Legs
scienceSources.evidence: Six wheels, three on each side; rocker-bogie suspension links the wheels and allows travel over rocks and depressions. The illustration uses a low obstacle and movable joints, not flexible metal supports or a claim that the body always stays perfectly level.

setting: Illustrative surface sequence on Mars, not a claim about a named historic drive. One Perseverance-type six-wheeled rover with white instrument body, gray camera mast, black and gray wheels and visible jointed suspension; dusty rust-red ground under a pale tan sky. No astronauts, plants, faces or flags.
props: One rover with exactly six wheels, three on each side
Jointed rocker-bogie suspension, not six independent telescoping legs
One low rounded gray rock, less than half wheel height
A shallow dip just beyond the rock
coverBrief: Three-quarter side view of the six-wheeled rover with its near front wheel on a low gray rock and the other near wheels on lower ground. Far wheels partly visible naturally; no invented seventh wheel.

pages.text:
This robot rolls across Mars.
It has six wheels.
pages.imageBrief: Three-quarter wide view establishes the rover on clear rough ground; three near wheels and the three far-side wheel positions are legible. Continuity: One rover, six wheels; gray obstacle lies ahead, not already beneath it.
pages.imageAlt: Three-quarter wide view establishes the rover on clear rough ground; three near wheels and the three far-side wheel positions are legible.
pages.pageDescription: Three-quarter wide view establishes the rover on clear rough ground; three near wheels and the three far-side wheel positions are legible.
pages.state: One rover, six wheels; gray obstacle lies ahead, not already beneath it.

pages.text:
Rocks lie ahead.
There is no smooth road.
pages.imageBrief: Lower near-side view places the small rounded gray rock in the front wheel’s path, with a shallow dip beyond it. Continuity: All three near wheels still before the obstacle; no paved road or tire track implying a human road.
pages.imageAlt: Lower near-side view places the small rounded gray rock in the front wheel’s path, with a shallow dip beyond it.
pages.pageDescription: Lower near-side view places the small rounded gray rock in the front wheel’s path, with a shallow dip beyond it.
pages.state: All three near wheels still before the obstacle; no paved road or tire track implying a human road.

pages.text: The front wheel climbs the small rock.
pages.imageBrief: Near front wheel rides onto the rock while middle and rear wheels remain on the lower ground behind it. Suspension pivots visibly. Continuity: Front wheel raised; middle and rear grounded; whole body tilts only modestly.
pages.imageAlt: Near front wheel rides onto the rock while middle and rear wheels remain on the lower ground behind it. Suspension pivots visibly.
pages.pageDescription: Near front wheel rides onto the rock while middle and rear wheels remain on the lower ground behind it. Suspension pivots visibly.

pages.text: The wheel supports bend at their joints.
pages.imageBrief: Closer view centers the rocker and bogie pivot geometry connecting all three near wheels; wheel height changes without rubbery metal bending. Continuity: Supports rotate at joints, not bend as soft rods; same front-wheel-on-rock moment continued.
pages.imageAlt: Closer view centers the rocker and bogie pivot geometry connecting all three near wheels; wheel height changes without rubbery metal bending.
pages.pageDescription: Closer view centers the rocker and bogie pivot geometry connecting all three near wheels; wheel height changes without rubbery metal bending.
pages.state: Supports rotate at joints, not bend as soft rods; same front-wheel-on-rock moment continued.

pages.text: Now the middle wheel rolls over the rock.
pages.imageBrief: Rover has advanced: near front wheel is beyond the rock, middle wheel sits on it and rear wheel remains behind. Continuity: Obstacle stays fixed on ground; suspension changes to the new wheel positions.
pages.imageAlt: Rover has advanced: near front wheel is beyond the rock, middle wheel sits on it and rear wheel remains behind.
pages.pageDescription: Rover has advanced: near front wheel is beyond the rock, middle wheel sits on it and rear wheel remains behind.
pages.state: Obstacle stays fixed on ground; suspension changes to the new wheel positions.

pages.text:
The back wheel follows.
The front wheel dips down.
pages.imageBrief: Near rear wheel crosses the rock while the near front wheel enters the shallow dip beyond; middle wheel is on the ground between. Continuity: Three wheel heights differ; natural articulated support keeps all near tires touching terrain.
pages.imageAlt: Near rear wheel crosses the rock while the near front wheel enters the shallow dip beyond; middle wheel is on the ground between.
pages.pageDescription: Near rear wheel crosses the rock while the near front wheel enters the shallow dip beyond; middle wheel is on the ground between.
pages.state: Three wheel heights differ; natural articulated support keeps all near tires touching terrain.

pages.text: The wheels come back onto level ground.
pages.imageBrief: The rover is beyond both obstacles; its near wheels align along a flatter patch. The same gray rock remains behind the rear wheel. Continuity: Rock crossing completed; no new rock substituted; six-wheel anatomy preserved.
pages.imageAlt: The rover is beyond both obstacles; its near wheels align along a flatter patch. The same gray rock remains behind the rear wheel.
pages.pageDescription: The rover is beyond both obstacles; its near wheels align along a flatter patch. The same gray rock remains behind the rear wheel.
pages.state: Rock crossing completed; no new rock substituted; six-wheel anatomy preserved.

pages.text:
The wheels rise and fall.
Joints help the rover cross rough ground.
pages.imageBrief: Wider final view shows the rover on the flatter patch, with its visible jointed wheel supports and the crossed uneven patch behind. Continuity: Outcome demonstrates the mechanism; no claim of perfectly level body, impossible terrain or human-like robot intention.
pages.imageAlt: Wider final view shows the rover on the flatter patch, with its visible jointed wheel supports and the crossed uneven patch behind.
pages.pageDescription: Wider final view shows the rover on the flatter patch, with its visible jointed wheel supports and the crossed uneven patch behind.
pages.state: Outcome demonstrates the mechanism; no claim of perfectly level body, impossible terrain or human-like robot intention.

oral.prompt: What moved when a wheel went up over the rock?
oral.listenFor: The linked supports changed angle at their joints, allowing wheels at different heights to keep contact with uneven ground.

visual.prompt: Which near wheel is on the rock now?
visual.lookFor: The middle wheel; front has passed it and rear has not reached it.

levelRationale: Candidate B: Concrete repeated wheel positions support a single physical sequence; no mission history, numerical speed or telecommunications load. Names for front/middle/back are spatially visible.

title: Is That a Twig?

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can a twiglike insect be recognized among real twigs?
storyBibleReview.progression: Begin with a concealed northern walkingstick, notice its legs and body resemblance, then use movement and feeding to distinguish it from the plant.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Twiglike shape helps conceal the animal, but its legs and feeding reveal a living insect.

scienceSources.title: Missouri Department of Conservation: Walkingsticks (Stick Insects)
scienceSources.evidence: Primary state field guide identifies northern walkingsticks, twiglike camouflage, six-legged insect form and leaf feeding. The book selects wingless adult Diapheromera femorata and does not generalize all stick insects as wingless or able to change color.

setting: One northern walkingstick, Diapheromera femorata, on a leafy deciduous branch in daylight. Adult wingless brown female with six legs, two long antennae and twiglike segmented body; natural compound eyes, no human face. Same forked twig and small oval leaves throughout.
props: One brown adult northern walkingstick, six legs and two antennae
One forked brown branch
One intact oval leaf that develops a small feeding notch
coverBrief: The walkingstick aligns its long body with one thin twig. Its six slim legs and two antennae are carefully distinguishable on inspection; show a real insect, not a branch growing legs.

pages.text: Is that a twig on the stem?
pages.imageBrief: Wide close-up hides the brown walkingstick along the branch fork. Its body color and narrow form blend with real twigs; all body parts remain natural. Continuity: Animal stationary; intact target leaf just ahead; exactly one insect.
pages.imageAlt: Wide close-up hides the brown walkingstick along the branch fork. Its body color and narrow form blend with real twigs; all body parts remain natural.
pages.pageDescription: Wide close-up hides the brown walkingstick along the branch fork. Its body color and narrow form blend with real twigs; all body parts remain natural.
pages.state: Animal stationary; intact target leaf just ahead; exactly one insect.

pages.text:
Look again.
Six legs grip the plant.
pages.imageBrief: A slightly closer angle reveals three pairs of slender legs attached to the insect’s thorax, gripping twigs at separate points. Continuity: Six legs total, plus two distinct antennae; no legs attached to abdomen or leaf.
pages.imageAlt: A slightly closer angle reveals three pairs of slender legs attached to the insect’s thorax, gripping twigs at separate points.
pages.pageDescription: A slightly closer angle reveals three pairs of slender legs attached to the insect’s thorax, gripping twigs at separate points.
pages.state: Six legs total, plus two distinct antennae; no legs attached to abdomen or leaf.

pages.text: A stick insect hides among twigs.
pages.imageBrief: Three-quarter view separates the long insect body visually from the branch while preserving its alignment and twiglike brown shape. Continuity: No change of color or body form; concealment comes from resemblance.
pages.imageAlt: Three-quarter view separates the long insect body visually from the branch while preserving its alignment and twiglike brown shape.
pages.pageDescription: Three-quarter view separates the long insect body visually from the branch while preserving its alignment and twiglike brown shape.
pages.state: No change of color or body form; concealment comes from resemblance.

pages.text: Its long brown body looks like a twig.
pages.imageBrief: Side view compares the insect’s narrow segmented outline with the adjacent real twig. Natural small head and antennae are visible. Continuity: Adult northern walkingstick remains wingless; no leaflike wings added.
pages.imageAlt: Side view compares the insect’s narrow segmented outline with the adjacent real twig. Natural small head and antennae are visible.
pages.pageDescription: Side view compares the insect’s narrow segmented outline with the adjacent real twig. Natural small head and antennae are visible.
pages.state: Adult northern walkingstick remains wingless; no leaflike wings added.

pages.text: Still legs are hard to spot among twigs.
pages.imageBrief: Wider view again places the motionless insect among several similar slim twigs, with the intact target leaf at its head end. Continuity: Same resting position; concealment is difficult spotting, not literal invisibility.
pages.imageAlt: Wider view again places the motionless insect among several similar slim twigs, with the intact target leaf at its head end.
pages.pageDescription: Wider view again places the motionless insect among several similar slim twigs, with the intact target leaf at its head end.
pages.state: Same resting position; concealment is difficult spotting, not literal invisibility.

pages.text:
One leg lifts.
The insect takes a slow step.
pages.imageBrief: One front leg reaches to a new grip ahead while five other legs support the body; antennae extend forward. Continuity: One leg in motion, not an extra seventh leg; insect advances toward target leaf.
pages.imageAlt: One front leg reaches to a new grip ahead while five other legs support the body; antennae extend forward.
pages.pageDescription: One front leg reaches to a new grip ahead while five other legs support the body; antennae extend forward.
pages.state: One leg in motion, not an extra seventh leg; insect advances toward target leaf.

pages.text: It reaches a leaf and takes a bite.
pages.imageBrief: The insect’s mouth meets the edge of the target leaf; a small fresh notch interrupts the smooth edge. Legs remain gripping the branch. Continuity: First visible feeding notch; no human teeth or chewing smile.
pages.imageAlt: The insect’s mouth meets the edge of the target leaf; a small fresh notch interrupts the smooth edge. Legs remain gripping the branch.
pages.pageDescription: The insect’s mouth meets the edge of the target leaf; a small fresh notch interrupts the smooth edge. Legs remain gripping the branch.
pages.state: First visible feeding notch; no human teeth or chewing smile.

pages.text:
Its shape helps it hide.
Its moving legs help us find it.
pages.imageBrief: Final view shows the walkingstick stepping beside the now notched leaf, its long body still matching the neighboring twigs. Continuity: Recognition combines earlier shape and motion clues; no predator outcome or universal promise of safety.
pages.imageAlt: Final view shows the walkingstick stepping beside the now notched leaf, its long body still matching the neighboring twigs.
pages.pageDescription: Final view shows the walkingstick stepping beside the now notched leaf, its long body still matching the neighboring twigs.
pages.state: Recognition combines earlier shape and motion clues; no predator outcome or universal promise of safety.

oral.prompt: What helped you decide this was not a twig?
oral.listenFor: The six legs, their movement and the feeding mouth; its shape still resembles real twigs.

visual.lookFor: A small bite notch appears at its edge beside the insect’s mouth.

levelRationale: Candidate B: The opening visual puzzle is answered through concrete observations, not a list of animal facts. Repeated familiar body/plant nouns support the limited new terms.

languagePrep.meaning: a thin woody part of a plant
hold on tightly
an animal with six legs and three main body parts

title: Ready for Wings

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How does a young grasshopper become able to fly?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow soil eggs, a wingless hatchling, feeding, repeated molts, wing-pad development and the final winged adult in chronological order.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The young hopper and winged adult are stages of the same kind of animal; wings develop during growth rather than appearing in an unrelated creature.

scienceSources.title: Utah State University Extension: Grasshoppers
scienceSources.evidence: Grasshoppers pass through egg, nymph and adult stages; flightless nymphs gradually develop wing pads and pass through molts. Species differ; this book depicts a common winged species rather than all grasshoppers.

scienceSources.title: Utah State University Extension: Grasshoppers, vegetable guide
scienceSources.evidence: Includes two-striped grasshopper; describes soil eggs, growing nymphs and increasing wing pads until winged adulthood. Supports selecting the illustrated species and keeping juvenile/adult anatomy connected.

setting: One illustrative two-striped grasshopper, Melanoplus bivittatus, across its egg, nymph and adult stages in a grassy field. Six legs, large rear jumping legs, two antennae, brown-green body with two pale lengthwise stripes; no butterfly chrysalis or caterpillar body.
props: Soil egg pod shown in a natural cutaway
One focal young grasshopper and its successive stages, never duplicate individuals in one scene
Grass blades with feeding notches
Empty shed outer skins distinct from live animals
coverBrief: One grown grasshopper with long folded wings rests on a grass blade; an empty shed skin clings lower on the stem. No second live juvenile or diagram collage.

pages.text: Grasshopper eggs lie in the soil.
pages.imageBrief: A natural side cutaway shows a grasshopper egg pod below a grassy field, with one focal egg nearest the upper opening. No grasshopper is on the surface yet. Continuity: Opening egg stage; one pod; no visible adult or winged offspring.
pages.imageAlt: A natural side cutaway shows a grasshopper egg pod below a grassy field, with one focal egg nearest the upper opening. No grasshopper is on the surface yet.
pages.pageDescription: A natural side cutaway shows a grasshopper egg pod below a grassy field, with one focal egg nearest the upper opening. No grasshopper is on the surface yet.
pages.state: Opening egg stage; one pod; no visible adult or winged offspring.

pages.text:
A small hopper comes out.
It has no long wings.
pages.imageBrief: One tiny grasshopper nymph emerges through the soil just above the opened pod; small grass blades and the same ground profile preserve location. Continuity: Hatching follows page 1; six legs, two antennae, large rear jumping legs and no full wings.
pages.imageAlt: One tiny grasshopper nymph emerges through the soil just above the opened pod; small grass blades and the same ground profile preserve location.
pages.pageDescription: One tiny grasshopper nymph emerges through the soil just above the opened pod; small grass blades and the same ground profile preserve location.
pages.state: Hatching follows page 1; six legs, two antennae, large rear jumping legs and no full wings.

pages.text:
It eats leaves.
Its body grows.
pages.imageBrief: Back at the field surface, the nymph feeds along a grass blade edge, leaving a small notch. Continuity: Back to young nymph stage; body remains wingless and smaller than final adult.
pages.imageAlt: Back at the field surface, the nymph feeds along a grass blade edge, leaving a small notch.
pages.pageDescription: Back at the field surface, the nymph feeds along a grass blade edge, leaving a small notch.
pages.state: Back to young nymph stage; body remains wingless and smaller than final adult.

pages.text:
Its tight outer skin splits.
The grasshopper pulls free.
pages.imageBrief: Nymph grips a stem while pulling its new pale body out of the split old exoskeleton; old leg casings hang below. Continuity: One live body and one empty casing, not two animals; no wings suddenly grown full-size.
pages.imageAlt: Nymph grips a stem while pulling its new pale body out of the split old exoskeleton; old leg casings hang below.
pages.pageDescription: Nymph grips a stem while pulling its new pale body out of the split old exoskeleton; old leg casings hang below.
pages.state: One live body and one empty casing, not two animals; no wings suddenly grown full-size.

pages.text:
It grows and sheds its skin again.
Small wing pads grow.
pages.imageBrief: A later, larger nymph rests beside an older empty casing; small wing pads are clearly present along its back. Continuity: Weeks of growth indicated by larger stage; no count or timing claim for every species.
pages.imageAlt: A later, larger nymph rests beside an older empty casing; small wing pads are clearly present along its back.
pages.pageDescription: A later, larger nymph rests beside an older empty casing; small wing pads are clearly present along its back.
pages.state: Weeks of growth indicated by larger stage; no count or timing claim for every species.

pages.text:
After the last shed,
long wings open and become firm.
pages.imageBrief: New adult clings to a stem with lengthening soft wings settling behind it; the last empty skin hangs separately below. Continuity: Final molt; wings not yet flying; maintain two wing pairs arranged naturally.
pages.imageAlt: New adult clings to a stem with lengthening soft wings settling behind it; the last empty skin hangs separately below.
pages.pageDescription: New adult clings to a stem with lengthening soft wings settling behind it; the last empty skin hangs separately below.
pages.state: Final molt; wings not yet flying; maintain two wing pairs arranged naturally.

pages.text: Now the grown grasshopper can fly.
pages.imageBrief: Adult grasshopper flies between two nearby grass stems, hind wings spread beneath the narrower forewings and six legs tucked naturally. Continuity: Adult flight stage; no extra insect or merged wings.
pages.imageAlt: Adult grasshopper flies between two nearby grass stems, hind wings spread beneath the narrower forewings and six legs tucked naturally.
pages.pageDescription: Adult grasshopper flies between two nearby grass stems, hind wings spread beneath the narrower forewings and six legs tucked naturally.
pages.state: Adult flight stage; no extra insect or merged wings.

pages.text:
The little hopper grows wings in stages.
Now it can hop and fly.
pages.imageBrief: The same adult rests with long wings folded along its striped body on the opening grass blade; an old small feeding notch remains nearby. Continuity: Ending identifies the winged adult as the result of the earlier egg and nymph stages; no claim every grasshopper species is winged.
pages.imageAlt: The same adult rests with long wings folded along its striped body on the opening grass blade; an old small feeding notch remains nearby.
pages.pageDescription: The same adult rests with long wings folded along its striped body on the opening grass blade; an old small feeding notch remains nearby.
pages.state: Ending identifies the winged adult as the result of the earlier egg and nymph stages; no claim every grasshopper species is winged.

oral.prompt: How does the small hopper become able to fly?
oral.listenFor: It feeds and grows through molts; wing pads develop into usable wings after the final shed.

visual.prompt: Can these small wing pads do the job of the final wings?
visual.lookFor: They are short developing pads; the long flying wings appear after the last shed.

levelRationale: Candidate B: One visible change answers the initial inability to fly. Short main clauses avoid a technical definition chain; nymph is oral preparation, while printed wing pads are pictured in context.

title: Can Light Get Through?

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Can three sheets be grouped by what happens to light and the view through them?
storyBibleReview.progression: Use the same flashlight and screen with clear plastic, wax paper and thick card; first group passing/blocking light, then distinguish clear from blurred views.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Testing reveals three useful groups even though all three materials began as similarly shaped sheets.

scienceSources.title: University of Waikato Science Learning Hub: Investigating shadows using transparent, translucent and opaque materials
scienceSources.evidence: Primary education investigation distinguishes passing most light, passing some scattered light and blocking light; transparent materials can still cast faint shadows. This book avoids equating clear with absolutely no shadow.

scienceSources.title: University of Waikato Science Learning Hub: Some materials let through more light than others do
scienceSources.evidence: Explains clear transmission versus scattering that blurs an object viewed through translucent material, and opaque materials blocking light. Supports the second split of the transmitting group.

setting: Dim but comfortable classroom table with one white screen. Same flashlight position, sample size and screen distance for comparisons. Room is not pitch black; no beam aimed at eyes.
props: One blue flashlight
One clear square plastic sheet
One same-sized square of translucent wax paper
One same-sized square of thick brown card
One white upright screen
One red toy car used for viewing through sheets
coverBrief: Kit holds clear plastic and Zoe holds wax paper at the table; the thick card stands separately. A single flashlight and white screen establish a comparison, with no invented labels or glowing material.

pages.text: Can light get through these three sheets?
pages.imageBrief: Three equal squares lie separately on the table: clear plastic, wax paper and thick brown card. Kit sets the flashlight before the white screen; red toy car sits aside. Continuity: All samples dry and unmarked; same sizes; no light test underway yet.
pages.imageAlt: Three equal squares lie separately on the table: clear plastic, wax paper and thick brown card. Kit sets the flashlight before the white screen; red toy car sits aside.
pages.pageDescription: Three equal squares lie separately on the table: clear plastic, wax paper and thick brown card. Kit sets the flashlight before the white screen; red toy car sits aside.
pages.state: All samples dry and unmarked; same sizes; no light test underway yet.

pages.text:
Kit shines a flashlight through clear plastic.
The wall stays bright.
pages.imageBrief: Kit holds clear plastic in the fixed light path between the flashlight and screen. A bright patch remains visible on the screen through it. Continuity: Plastic transmits most light; faint edge effects allowed; no claim perfectly invisible or shadowless.
pages.imageAlt: Kit holds clear plastic in the fixed light path between the flashlight and screen. A bright patch remains visible on the screen through it.
pages.pageDescription: Kit holds clear plastic in the fixed light path between the flashlight and screen. A bright patch remains visible on the screen through it.
pages.state: Plastic transmits most light; faint edge effects allowed; no claim perfectly invisible or shadowless.

pages.text:
Zoe holds up wax paper.
A soft glow shows through.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe replaces the plastic with wax paper in the same holder position. The paper glows diffusely and the screen light is softer. Continuity: Only sample changes; flashlight and screen distance fixed; plastic lies aside.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe replaces the plastic with wax paper in the same holder position. The paper glows diffusely and the screen light is softer.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe replaces the plastic with wax paper in the same holder position. The paper glows diffusely and the screen light is softer.
pages.state: Only sample changes; flashlight and screen distance fixed; plastic lies aside.

pages.text:
Now she holds thick card.
A dark patch covers the wall.
pages.imageBrief: The thick card occupies the light path and blocks its center, producing a defined dark patch on the white screen. Continuity: Opaque card blocks visible light; room remains lit enough to see children and equipment.
pages.imageAlt: The thick card occupies the light path and blocks its center, producing a defined dark patch on the white screen.
pages.pageDescription: The thick card occupies the light path and blocks its center, producing a defined dark patch on the white screen.
pages.state: Opaque card blocks visible light; room remains lit enough to see children and equipment.

pages.text:
Zoe puts the card in one group.
It blocks the light.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe lays the card alone on the left of the table. Plastic and wax paper remain to the right beside the switched-off flashlight. Continuity: Two provisional groups will form; only one card; no labels needed.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe lays the card alone on the left of the table. Plastic and wax paper remain to the right beside the switched-off flashlight.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe lays the card alone on the left of the table. Plastic and wax paper remain to the right beside the switched-off flashlight.
pages.state: Two provisional groups will form; only one card; no labels needed.

pages.text:
The plastic and wax paper go together.
Both let light through.
pages.imageBrief: Kit places plastic and wax paper side by side in the right-hand group, with a clear gap separating them from the lone card. Continuity: First grouping: one blocking sheet versus two transmitting sheets.
pages.imageAlt: Kit places plastic and wax paper side by side in the right-hand group, with a clear gap separating them from the lone card.
pages.pageDescription: Kit places plastic and wax paper side by side in the right-hand group, with a clear gap separating them from the lone card.
pages.state: First grouping: one blocking sheet versus two transmitting sheets.

pages.text:
Kit looks through both.
One gives a clear view. One blurs it.

title: One Little Drip

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Zoe notices a faucet still dripping after it is closed; Kit’s extra turn fails, so they catch the water and ask a grown-up to repair the leak.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Turning the closed handle a little farther does not stop the drip; catching it makes the continuing loss visible.
storyBibleReview.resolution: An adult repairs the internal part with the supply off; the restored supply and closed-faucet test confirm no drip, and the caught water is used for a plant.

scienceSources.title: US Environmental Protection Agency WaterSense: Fix a Leak Week
scienceSources.evidence: Worn faucet washers or gaskets can cause drips, and leaks waste water. The agency specifies turning off the supply before repair. This story depicts one compression faucet whose worn washer is the identified cause, not a universal faucet fix.

setting: Ordinary classroom sink with one compression-style faucet and an accessible adult-operated shutoff below; nearby potted leafy plant. Grown-up has medium brown skin, short dark wavy hair, a green long-sleeved shirt and dark trousers. Children observe; adult alone uses tools.
props: One silver faucet with a rounded handle
One yellow cup below the spout
One small black worn rubber washer and matching new washer
One adult-held wrench
One potted leafy plant on the nearby sill
coverBrief: Zoe shows a yellow cup partly filled by drips beneath the closed faucet. Kit stands beside her and the grown-up looks toward the source. Focus on small drops accumulating, not a flood.

pages.text:
Zoe turns the faucet off.
A drop still falls.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe has moved the handle to its closed position. One drop hangs under the silver spout above the empty sink. Continuity: Faucet closed but leaking; yellow cup still on the counter.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe has moved the handle to its closed position. One drop hangs under the silver spout above the empty sink.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe has moved the handle to its closed position. One drop hangs under the silver spout above the empty sink.
pages.state: Faucet closed but leaking; yellow cup still on the counter.

pages.text:
Kit tries the handle.
Drip. It still leaks.
pages.imageBrief: Kit gives the closed handle a small gentle turn, not forcing it with tools. Another drop falls from the spout. Continuity: First attempt fails; no changed water pressure or broken handle.
pages.imageAlt: Kit gives the closed handle a small gentle turn, not forcing it with tools. Another drop falls from the spout.
pages.pageDescription: Kit gives the closed handle a small gentle turn, not forcing it with tools. Another drop falls from the spout.
pages.state: First attempt fails; no changed water pressure or broken handle.

pages.text:
Zoe puts a cup below it.
Drip, drip, drip.
pages.imageBrief: Yellow cup sits directly under the spout; a few drops have begun collecting inside. Zoe and Kit watch. Continuity: Same slow leak; cup starts nearly empty, no instant full cup.
pages.imageAlt: Yellow cup sits directly under the spout; a few drops have begun collecting inside. Zoe and Kit watch.
pages.pageDescription: Yellow cup sits directly under the spout; a few drops have begun collecting inside. Zoe and Kit watch.
pages.state: Same slow leak; cup starts nearly empty, no instant full cup.

pages.text:
The cup is half full.
Zoe shows the leak to a grown-up.
pages.imageBrief: Later, the yellow cup is half full. Zoe points to the continuing drip while the grown-up crouches beside the sink. Continuity: Elapsed time; cup exactly half full, not overflowing; faucet remains closed but leaking.
pages.imageAlt: Later, the yellow cup is half full. Zoe points to the continuing drip while the grown-up crouches beside the sink.
pages.pageDescription: Later, the yellow cup is half full. Zoe points to the continuing drip while the grown-up crouches beside the sink.
pages.state: Elapsed time; cup exactly half full, not overflowing; faucet remains closed but leaking.

pages.text:
The grown-up shuts off the water.
She fits a new part.
pages.imageBrief: Adult alone works on the opened faucet after turning off its supply. The worn black washer rests on a small dry cloth; she fits its matching replacement. Continuity: Supply off; no running spout during dismantling; children stand back; cup of caught water stays intact on counter.
pages.imageAlt: Adult alone works on the opened faucet after turning off its supply. The worn black washer rests on a small dry cloth; she fits its matching replacement.
pages.pageDescription: Adult alone works on the opened faucet after turning off its supply. The worn black washer rests on a small dry cloth; she fits its matching replacement.
pages.state: Supply off; no running spout during dismantling; children stand back; cup of caught water stays intact on counter.

pages.text:
She turns the water back on.
Kit tests the faucet.
pages.imageBrief: Faucet is reassembled; adult finishes opening the supply below while Kit opens the faucet and a normal stream runs into the sink. Continuity: Repair complete before supply returns; yellow cup remains on counter, not discarded down drain.
pages.imageAlt: Faucet is reassembled; adult finishes opening the supply below while Kit opens the faucet and a normal stream runs into the sink.
pages.pageDescription: Faucet is reassembled; adult finishes opening the supply below while Kit opens the faucet and a normal stream runs into the sink.
pages.state: Repair complete before supply returns; yellow cup remains on counter, not discarded down drain.

pages.text:
He closes it. They wait.
No drops fall.
pages.imageBrief: Kit’s hand rests away from the closed handle. Zoe and adult watch the dry spout; the sink below is not receiving any drops. Continuity: Test after restored supply confirms repair; no suggestion stopping supply alone fixed leak.
pages.imageAlt: Kit’s hand rests away from the closed handle. Zoe and adult watch the dry spout; the sink below is not receiving any drops.
pages.pageDescription: Kit’s hand rests away from the closed handle. Zoe and adult watch the dry spout; the sink below is not receiving any drops.
pages.state: Test after restored supply confirms repair; no suggestion stopping supply alone fixed leak.

pages.text:
Zoe waters a plant with the saved water.
The cup stays empty.
pages.imageBrief: Zoe holds the now empty yellow cup beside the potted plant, whose soil has just been watered. The closed faucet is visible behind her without a drop. Continuity: Caught water has been used on the plant; cup empty; no new drips refill it; no plant flooding.
pages.imageAlt: Zoe holds the now empty yellow cup beside the potted plant, whose soil has just been watered. The closed faucet is visible behind her without a drop.
pages.pageDescription: Zoe holds the now empty yellow cup beside the potted plant, whose soil has just been watered. The closed faucet is visible behind her without a drop.
pages.state: Caught water has been used on the plant; cup empty; no new drips refill it; no plant flooding.

oral.prompt: How did they check that the repair worked?
oral.listenFor: The grown-up restored the supply; Kit ran and closed the faucet; they waited and saw no new drops.

visual.prompt: Who is fixing the faucet, and where is the saved water?
visual.lookFor: The grown-up uses the tool with the supply off; the yellow cup remains safely on the counter.

levelRationale: Candidate B: Two short clauses at a time track a practical failed attempt, help-seeking and verified repair. No procedural instruction asks a child to handle plumbing; the visible cup gives meaning to the small leak.
